title: Shared target groups exceeded spatial count controls in two adult worm maps
abstract: We tested whether target pairs at shared chemical synaptic sites repeat between two adult C. elegans maps beyond local target counts. We reused 162 neurons and 6421 sites. The cross-map count-product score was 10119. Controls preserved site target counts and target incidence counts within each source and spatial cluster. With up to four clusters per source, control means were 7317.9 and 7143.3 when each adult was changed in turn. Observed-to-mean ratios were 1.383 and 1.417. Both finite-chain upper ranks were 1/399. With sixteen clusters, ratios fell to 1.124 and 1.161; many sites then could not change. Spatial constraints explain part of the excess under count-only controls. A residual remains under the tested constraints. Exact contact geometry, two animals, partial coverage and finite-chain sampling limit inference. No activity or shared release was measured. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records remain outside this baseline package.

display.caption: Cross-map target-group score under three spatial count controls. Bars give central 95% finite-chain ranges, not animal confidence intervals.
